title: WEIRD Audits? Research Trends, Linguistic and Geographical Disparities in the Algorithm Audits of Online Platforms - A Systematic Literature Review

bias_targets.methodology: Systematically reviewing 176 algorithm audit studies to extract the target country contexts and author affiliations, comparing these to global demographics to identify a disproportionate focus on WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic) countries, particularly the US.

Coding the language of the content analyzed in 176 algorithm audits and comparing these frequencies to the global distribution of language speakers and internet content, demonstrating a massive skew toward English-language research.

Extracting and categorizing the group-based attributes (such as gender, race, age, sexuality, and religion) evaluated in the 176 reviewed algorithm audits to reveal the field's narrow focus on a limited set of attributes, which are often operationalized as simplistic binaries.

Quantifying the frequency of specific platforms audited in the 176 reviewed papers to highlight an overrepresentation of major Western platforms (like Google Search and YouTube) while neglecting other globally or regionally significant platforms.
